title: No-code SDK quickstart guide + labs (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a no-code quickstart and lab set aimed at product managers, designers, customer success managers, and engineers who want to prototype Redwood Inference flows without writing backend code. Goal is: 10–15 minute first success, repeatable lab exercises, and clear handoffs to eng if they want to productionize.

Audience & personas:
- PM/Designer persona: wants to validate conversational UX quickly with stakeholders.
- CS/Pre-sales persona: build a demo for a prospect with customer-specific prompts.
- Citizen dev / BI persona: wire up embeddings->search in Sheets/Retool.
- Engineer (shadowing): validates integration surface and telemetry events.

What success looks like (lab outcomes):
- User wires Zapier -> Redwood hosted API to generate content from a Google Form submission.
- User configures a Google Sheets row -> embeddings -> simple similarity lookup using a Make/Make.com scenario or Zapier multi-step.
- User produces a shareable link/demo and records token/cost estimate.
- UX validated with 3 internal reviewers; acceptance checklist passed.

Core sections to ship in the quickstart pack (short bullets):
- 1-pager: Why no-code + constraints (latency, token cost, data residency).
- Pre-req checklist: API key, free credits, example dataset (CSV), Zapier/Make account, sample Sheet + Form.
- Step-by-step lab 1: "Auto-Reply from Form" (Zapier)
- Step-by-step lab 2: "FAQ lookup with embeddings" (Sheets + Make/Retool)
- Telemetry & cost quick-check: event names, sample Mini-dashboard in Sheets.
- Fallbacks & safety: rate limits, prompt injection note, PII redaction pattern.
- Handoff template to eng: spec + minimal prod checklist.

Lab 1: Auto-Reply from Google Form (Zapier) — 10–15 min
- Goal: Build a Zap that listens to a form, calls Redwood generate, and emails a reply.
- Steps (concise):
  1) Create sample Form: fields: name, issue summary.
  2) Zapier trigger: New Google Form response (connect account).
  3) Add action: Webhooks by Zapier -> POST to Redwood /v1/chat or /v1/generate.
     - Example body (JSON):
       {
         "model": "redwood-1.1",
         "prompt": "Reply to: {{issue_summary}} with a friendly triage note. Keep under 80 words."
       }
  4) Send Email action: Use generated text in email body.
- Test cases to run: short summary, long summary, malicious input (script tags).
- Notes: Show how to add a simple prefix cache by caching the last 20 responses in a Sheet for quick manual review.

Lab 2: FAQ lookup with embeddings (Google Sheets + Make) — 20–30 min
- Goal: Use a small FAQ CSV to build embeddings in a Sheet and do a similarity-based answer lookup.
- Steps (concise):
  1) Provide sample FAQ CSV (Title, Q, A).
  2) Make scenario: scheduled run or Sheet change -> for each row call /v1/embeddings to get vector and persist in a hidden column.
  3) When end-user question arrives (Form or Sheet cell), call /v1/embeddings for the query, compute cosine similarity across stored vectors (simple JS snippet in Make or in-sheet formula via script).
  4) If highest similarity > threshold (e.g., 0.75) return existing A; else call /v1/generate with retrieved context.
- Heuristics: If top similarity is 0.6–0.75, return candidate answers with a "confidence" flag for human review.
- Edge cases: authentication expiration in Sheets connector, rate limiting when embedding > 50 rows at once.

Telemetry & lightweight metrics (what the no-code user can track easily):
- Events we recommend emitting from the integration (Zapier/Make step metadata):
  - rc_no_code.triggered (form_id, user_email)
  - rc_no_code.request_sent (endpoint, model, tokens_estimate)
  - rc_no_code.response_received (latency_ms, status)
  - rc_no_code.fallback_used (reason)
- Minimal dashboard (Sheet tabs): Requests (timestamp, prompt summary, tokens, cost_est), Errors, Cost by model, Sample outputs (for QA).

Token cost quick estimate method (sheet-friendly):
- For generative quickstarts assume average 120 tokens/request. Multiply by 0.0004 USD per token (example pricing) and show cost-per-1000-req estimate. Include example row and formula.

Safety / data handling quick notes (short):
- No-code flows commonly move PII into third-party apps; call this out on the first page.
- Include a one-liner for on-prem/Dedicated option: "For sensitive data use Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments — see linked artifact."
- Add a small red-box checklist for testers: sanitize sample data, include injection cases, strip HTML.

Test matrix (very lightweight to include in lab):
- Persona | Input length | Expected | Pass criteria
- PM | 1–2 sentence | Friendly reply | Human review OK
- CS | long form (300+ words) | Short summary | <=80 words + accurate
- Analyst | search query | Matching FAQ answer | similarity > 0.75 or fallback triggered

Handoff to engineering (one-paragraph template to paste):
- "We built a no-code proof-of-concept using Zapier + Redwood hosted API. Main flows: auto-reply and FAQ-lookup. Expected QPS low (<5). Key constraints: current Zapier webhook sends API key from user account (replace with service account), need to add server-side rate limiting, token-level telemetry, and per-tenant prompt templates. See attached sheet with sample prompts/outputs and the minimal event list for telemetry."

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Do we want a branded Zapier app for Redwood (vs. webhook pattern) for better UX and token management?
- Create a sanitized 100-row FAQ dataset for workshops.
- Workshop script: 45-minute facilitator guide (slides + checklist).
- Should we include a Retool prebuilt app for the embedding lookup? (useful for enterprise demos)

Appendix: quick snippets and troubleshooting tips
- Example curl (Zapier webhook body):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1","prompt":"Reply to: What is my refund status? Keep it concise."}'

- Common failures and fixes:
  - 401 Unauthorized: check that Zapier webhook includes Authorization header; rotate key in a single place.
  - 429 Rate limit: batch or add exponential backoff in Make; for critical demos switch to a dedicated key.
  - Weird outputs: add system-level instruction prefix and small temperature (0.0–0.2).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight and biased toward speed-of-experiment. We should ship a one-pager + two lab worksheets + the sample Sheet. Post-facilitator feedback will inform a polished "no-code kit" release.

-- end of sketch --
